events.label: Trim attitude, heat shield forward, 120 km
Parachute cover off, pilot and drogue chutes, 10 km

inputs.name: Shenzhou-20
inputs.description: Uncrewed return of the Shenzhou-20 spacecraft (cracked window) from the China Space Station to the Dongfeng landing site, 19 January 2026.

tle.name: SZ-20
tle.source: Space-Track gp_history for NORAD 63632 (SZ-20); epoch 2026-01-19 00:56:12 UTC, the last element set consistent with the pre-burn orbit (mean motion follows the decay trend of the previous sets; the 17:50 UTC set is a post-landing propagation artefact).

sources: CMSA / Xinhua 2026-01-19: undocked 00:23 Beijing (18 Jan 16:23 UTC), return capsule landed 09:34 Beijing (01:34 UTC) at the Dongfeng landing site.
CCTV 2026-01-19 video report: orbital module separated 08:44 Beijing (00:44 UTC), then deorbit engine burn, service-module separation, landing 09:34.
Landing coordinates 41 39 13 N 100 45 13 E from the Wikipedia Shenzhou 20 article (unverified against CMSA).
Terrain height about 1.0 km (Jiuquan / Ejin Banner Gobi, 940-1100 m); assumption.
reported.landing_time_note: Reported to the minute (09:34 Beijing); mid-minute used, tolerance +/-30 s.
reported.om_separation_note: Reported to the minute (08:44 Beijing); the burn follows a ~60 s attitude slew.

design.gamma_note: Entry flight-path angle target (inertial). CASC explainers give 1.5-1.7 deg without stating the reference height; 120 km (trim-attitude height) is used, which corresponds to about 1.9 deg at 100 km.
design.burn_note: Published 150-180 s; constant thrust acceleration, retrograde along the inertial velocity (no pitch).
sequence_sources: CCTV / Xinhua return-sequence explainers (Shenzhou-14, -16, -20): orbital-module separation, two 90-degree attitude slews (~120 s), retro burn 150-180 s, service-module separation at ~145 km, trim attitude at ~120 km, entry at ~100 km at ~7 km/s, blackout 80-40 km, speed ~200 m/s at 10 km, pilot/drogue/main chutes from 10 km, main 1200 m2 giving 7-8 m/s, heat shield jettison at ~6 km, retro-rockets at 1 m, touchdown 1-2 m/s.

sources: Return module 3,240 kg, 2.52 m diameter, hypersonic L/D 0.30 (astronautix.com, braeunig.us Shenzhou specifications).
Service module 3,000 kg at launch with 1,000 kg propellant, main engine 10 kN (4 x 2.5 kN), Isp 290 s; 2,500 kg assumed at deorbit after 270 days.

Parachutes: pilot 4.25 + 0.7 m2, drogue 24 m2, main 1,200 m2 ring-sail, backup 760 m2 (China Space Report). Drogue Cd 0.8; main Cd*S 920 m2 chosen so the descent rate is 7.5 m/s at the 1 km site elevation with the 2,940 kg post-shield mass.
Hypersonic Cd 1.30 for a Soyuz-class blunt capsule at its trim angle (modified Newtonian); ballistic coefficient ~500 kg/m2.

solver.t_ign_note: Fixed per run: reported orbital-module separation 08:44 Beijing (minute precision) plus the ~60-90 s second attitude slew gives 00:45:00-00:46:30 UTC; the README scans this range.
